To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

three novel mutations of NOG have been identified in three Spanish patients with FOP; these mutations, as well the Delta42 deletion reported previously, result in the alteration of a potential N-myristylation site of noggin; and the three mutations, as the Delta42, are de novo, suggesting that FOP results from a de novo dominant negative mutation in the noggin locus.

we report three novel mutations of noggin gene (G92R, G91C, G92E) in Spanish FOP patients and that all three mutations result in the alteration of a potential N-myristylation site at residues 91-GGGGGA.
we report the identification of three novel mutations (G91C, G92R and G92E) in the NOG gene of three Spanish patients with fibrodyslplasia ossificants progressiva.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the first report of the identification of three novel mutations at nucleotides 274 (G to C), 271 (G to T) and 275 (G to A), encoding for the corresponding G92R, G91C and G92E substitutions at the peptide level, respectively.
the first report of three novel mutations in the NOG gene of patients with FOP, and with the first description of a partially affected father.
the identification of novel mutations in the NOG gene that may be useful in the diagnosis of FOP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the three novel missense mutations of the NOG, as well as Delta42 deletion, are associated with FOP, and that the potential N-myrisoylation site at the N-terminal region of NOG is crucial for the normal function of this protein.
mutations in the NOG gene, in the region encoding for residues 89-94, result in the development of FOP.
all mutations reported in patients with FOP are located within the region 265-282 of the NOG coding sequence and are associated with a potential myristoylation site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutations identified here, as well as other mutations reported in the literature, are all located in the same region of the NOG protein.
all four mutations of the NOG reported so far are located at the N-myristoylating site, which is a key site for protein-protein interactions.

all the mutations identified in the NOG gene of FOP patients, as well as in the corresponding animal models, are clustered at a region encoding for the potential myristoylation site of the NOG peptide, suggesting a role of this site in the pathogenesis of FOP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GGGGGA motif at residues 89-94 of the noggin protein is a crucial element in the pathogenesis of FOP.
, in addition to the Delta42 mutation, three novel mutations of NOG have been identified, all of them resulting in the alteration of this N-myristoylated site.
the three novel missense mutations identified in this study, as well as that already reported in the literature, are all localized at a specific portion of the noggin molecule.
